identity.title: Antibiotic exposure within 8-12 weeks plus new watery diarrhea (>=3/day) or ileus/distension

technique.how: Ask about any antibiotic course in the preceding 12 weeks (name, dates), recent hospitalization, proton-pump inhibitor use, and prior C. difficile infection. Establish stool frequency and consistency (>=3 unformed stools in 24 h) and, in a patient with distension and few stools, consider ileus/toxic megacolon; examine for abdominal distension, tenderness and fever.
technique.prerequisites: Review the medication administration record and outside records; exclude laxative use and tube-feed related diarrhea.

interpretation.positive_finding: Recent antibiotics plus new unformed stools >=3/day meets the guideline case definition for testing and should prompt a C. difficile stool test and contact precautions; distension with ileus and leukocytosis suggests fulminant disease.
interpretation.negative_finding: No antibiotic exposure and neither significant diarrhea nor abdominal pain identified a low-risk group in Katz's cohort in whom cytotoxin assays were rarely positive, though community-acquired CDI without antibiotic exposure occurs.
interpretation.pitfalls: Laxatives, tube feeds and other drugs cause hospital diarrhea; testing formed stool yields colonization, not infection. Ileus can mask diarrhea entirely in the sickest patients.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: send C. difficile testing, start contact isolation, review antibiotics/PPIs. Negative: pursue other causes of diarrhea; testing rarely positive.

sources.citation: McDonald LC, Gerding DN, Johnson S, Bakken JS, Carroll KC, Coffin SE, Dubberke ER, Garey KW, et al. Clinical Practice Guidelines for Clostridium difficile Infection in Adults and Children: 2017 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA). Clin Infect Dis. 2018.
Katz DA, Bates DW, Rittenberg E, Onderdonk A, Sands K, Barefoot LA, Snydman D. Predicting Clostridium difficile stool cytotoxin results in hospitalized patients with diarrhea. J Gen Intern Med. 1997.

Garey KW, Dao-Tran TK, Jiang ZD, Price MP, Gentry LO, Dupont HL. A clinical risk index for Clostridium difficile infection in hospitalised patients receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics. J Hosp Infect. 2008.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not require an antibiotic history before testing a patient with severe or bloody diarrhea, or one with ileus/distension and marked leukocytosis after recent hospitalization.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hypotension, ileus, megacolon or WBC >15 with rising creatinine indicates severe/fulminant CDI needing urgent treatment and surgical awareness.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: History elements are self-reported or chart-derived; no reliability data found.

extraction_notes: No diagnostic-accuracy (sens/spec/LR) estimate for the history element itself was found in accessible abstracts, so status is not_quantified. Katz 1997 (prospective cohort, 609 inpatients tested for cytotoxin): low-risk group defined as no prior antibiotic use and no symptom predictor had 'the misclassification rate was 2.8% (5/177) for assay results' and 'prevalence of positive cytotoxin assays was 8% in the validation set, compared with 14% in the derivation set' (Abstract); a 2x2 cannot be reconstructed from the abstract, so no estimate entered. Garey 2008 reports risk-index odds ratios (e.g. age >80 OR 2.5, non-surgical admission OR 2.2; Abstract) for developing CDI among antibiotic recipients - prognostic risk, not diagnostic accuracy. IDSA/SHEA 2017 guideline provides the case definition (>=3 unformed stools in 24 h; test only unformed stool). Stool-frequency threshold in the title is from that guideline (full text not consulted; case definition is unverified recall of exact wording).
